issues.label: Sufficiency: aggravated sexual assault 1
issues.why: Court must determine whether evidence proved each element beyond a reasonable doubt for the first aggravated sexual assault count.

issues.label: Sufficiency: aggravated sexual assault 2
issues.why: Court must determine whether evidence proved each element beyond a reasonable doubt for the second aggravated sexual assault count.

issues.label: Separate-act proof for two assaults
issues.why: Court must decide whether the two aggravated sexual assault counts were based on distinct acts (oral vs anal) supporting separate convictions.

issues.label: Aggravators for sexual assault
issues.why: Court must ensure the charged aggravating circumstances (e.g., weapon, serious bodily injury, kidnapping/force) were proven as required by statute.

issues.label: Sufficiency: aggravated assault
issues.why: Court must decide whether the evidence supported all elements of aggravated assault (including use of a dangerous weapon or serious bodily injury/strangulation as applicable).

issues.label: Dangerous weapon definition
issues.why: Court must determine whether a pocketknife qualifies as a dangerous weapon under the charged theory and instructions.

issues.label: Strangulation evidence and element
issues.why: Court must assess whether the neck-grab/strangulation evidence satisfies any charged element or aggravator (and jury instruction alignment).

issues.label: Sufficiency: aggravated robbery (keys)
issues.why: Court must decide whether taking the car keys was accomplished by force/threat and with intent to steal, meeting aggravated robbery elements.

issues.label: Property interest in car keys
issues.why: Court must confirm that car keys constitute property capable of being the subject of robbery under Utah law.

issues.label: Timing nexus for robbery
issues.why: Court must address whether threats/force were sufficiently contemporaneous with the taking of keys to constitute robbery.

issues.label: Intent to permanently deprive
issues.why: Court must decide whether Connelley intended to deprive Jessica of the keys (or substantially appropriate) as required for theft/robbery intent.

issues.label: Sufficiency: credit card acquisition counts
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether evidence proved unlawful acquisition of each credit card and the required mental state.

issues.label: Unit of prosecution—cards
issues.why: Court must determine whether each credit card supports a separate count or whether multiple cards acquired in one episode constitute one offense.

issues.label: Merger: cards into robbery
issues.why: Court must decide whether unlawful acquisition of credit cards is a lesser-included or otherwise merges into aggravated robbery under Utah merger principles.

issues.label: Merger analysis framework
issues.why: Court must apply Utah’s merger/lesser-included tests (elements, evidence, legislative intent) to the robbery and card offenses.

issues.label: Double jeopardy protections
issues.why: Court must ensure multiple convictions/punishments do not violate federal or Utah double jeopardy clauses.

issues.label: Multiplicity in charging
issues.why: Court must consider whether the three credit-card counts are multiplicitous, risking multiple punishments for one act.

issues.label: Inconsistent verdict concerns
issues.why: Court must address any claim that convictions are logically inconsistent given competing consent narratives and theft intent testimony.

issues.label: Jury instruction correctness
issues.why: Court must ensure instructions correctly stated elements, mental states, definitions, and burdens for all charges.

issues.label: Consent and force instructions
issues.why: Court must ensure jury was properly instructed on consent, lack of consent, and force/threat in sexual offenses.

issues.label: Credibility and impeachment limits
issues.why: Court must decide whether any evidentiary rulings improperly restricted impeachment/credibility evidence affecting the verdict.

issues.label: Admissibility of prior bad acts
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether any evidence of Connelley’s prior criminal history was admitted at trial and, if so, whether it complied with Rule 404(b)/403 and due process.

issues.label: Prosecutorial misconduct in argument
issues.why: Court must consider whether the State’s rhetoric (e.g., lifelong victimizer) improperly appealed to passion or relied on facts not in evidence at trial.

issues.label: Right to present defense
issues.why: Court must ensure defense was allowed to present consent narrative and relevant evidence without unconstitutional restriction.

issues.label: Sufficiency vs weight of evidence
issues.why: Court must distinguish legal sufficiency review from any claim the verdict was against the weight of the evidence.

issues.label: Sentencing range legality
issues.why: Court must confirm each imposed sentence fell within statutory minimums/maximums and was authorized for the offense level.

issues.label: 15-to-life sentencing basis
issues.why: Court must verify the court’s stated view about minimums for aggravated sexual assault aligned with statutory ranges and did not reflect legal error.

issues.label: Consecutive sentencing authority
issues.why: Court must determine whether Utah law authorized consecutive sentences for these counts and the required findings/considerations.

issues.label: Consecutive to other cases
issues.why: Court must confirm authority and procedure for ordering sentences consecutive to sentences in other criminal cases.

issues.label: Sentencing discretion abuse
issues.why: Court must decide whether the court abused discretion by relying on improper factors or failing to consider required factors.

issues.label: Sentencing factors considered
issues.why: Court must ensure the court considered gravity/circumstances, defendant’s history/character, and rehabilitative needs as required by Utah law.

issues.label: Victim impact consideration limits
issues.why: Court must ensure victim-impact testimony was considered appropriately and did not introduce improper or unreliable information driving the sentence.

issues.label: Punishment for lack of remorse
issues.why: Court must decide whether the court permissibly considered lack of remorse/credibility without penalizing exercise of trial rights.

issues.label: Due process in sentencing facts
issues.why: Court must ensure sentencing was not based on materially false or unreliable information, consistent with due process.

issues.label: PSI inaccuracies preservation
issues.why: Court must determine whether defense sufficiently preserved objections to PSI inaccuracies and requested rulings.

issues.label: PSI findings requirement
issues.why: Court must decide whether the court was required to make findings or resolve disputed PSI statements before sentencing.

issues.label: Rule compliance for PSI disputes
issues.why: Court must apply Utah procedural rules governing presentence report objections, corrections, and record-keeping.

issues.label: Harm from PSI errors
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether alleged PSI inaccuracies were material and prejudicial to sentencing outcome.

issues.label: Record correction/remand remedy
issues.why: Court must determine appropriate remedy if PSI disputes were not resolved (e.g., remand for findings, resentencing, PSI amendment).

issues.label: Use of juvenile history
issues.why: Court must address whether and how juvenile adjudications may be considered at sentencing under Utah law and due process.

issues.label: Consideration of uncharged conduct
issues.why: Court must determine whether the court relied on uncharged/alleged conduct (e.g., “victimized people constantly”) and whether reliance was proper and supported.

issues.label: Age and proportionality
issues.why: Court must consider any claim that consecutive sentences amount to de facto life and raise proportionality/cruel punishment concerns.

issues.label: Utah constitution proportionality
issues.why: Court must analyze any Utah constitutional challenge to sentence severity compared to offense and offender characteristics.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment proportionality
issues.why: Court must analyze any federal proportionality claim for an aggregate consecutive sentence.

issues.label: Aggregate sentence reasonableness
issues.why: Court must consider whether the overall consecutive structure was justified and not arbitrary given stated purposes.

issues.label: Credit-card counts sentencing
issues.why: Court must ensure separate sentences for each unlawful acquisition count are lawful if counts do not merge.

issues.label: Restitution eligibility and basis
issues.why: Court must determine whether restitution is required/appropriate and supported by evidence (even if not described, it is a common sentencing component).

issues.label: Crime victim rights compliance
issues.why: Court must ensure victim’s rights to be heard and to receive notice were satisfied and did not prejudice defendant’s rights.

issues.label: Clerical accuracy of judgment
issues.why: Court must confirm the written judgment correctly reflects counts, degrees, enhancements, consecutive/concurrent structure, and credits.

issues.label: Presentence jail credit
issues.why: Court must verify calculation and award of any custody credit to avoid illegal sentence issues.

issues.label: Preservation of merger claim
issues.why: Court must determine whether merger/double-jeopardy arguments were properly preserved at trial for appellate review.

issues.label: Standard of review selection
issues.why: Court must identify correct standards (e.g., correctness for merger, abuse of discretion for sentencing, plain error if unpreserved).

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: Court must decide whether any identified error affected the outcome (verdict or sentence) or was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt/under Utah standard.
